title: Read: near
description: What is at, or within a radius of, one terrain node. Answered by POST /world/near (Sim/icarus_sim/terrain_read.near_request). Distances are great-circle metres on effective_config.globe_radius, measured with the expression terrain_erosion.sphere_grid uses for a node's neighbours. Two things standing on one node are at distance exactly zero, read off the node the writer stored rather than off an arc length.

node.description: The terrain node asked about. Nodes are numbered 0..n-1 over terrain_erosion.sphere_grid's point list and are the one identifier in this tree that does not renumber at an age boundary.

radius_ceiling_m.description: Half this world's globe radius, the same relative bound terrain_patch puts on a patch span. A larger radius_m is refused as refused_by_world.

row_ceiling.description: Rows past which the read refuses with STATE_CAPACITY rather than truncating. A truncated answer to 'what is near here' is a wrong answer that looks complete.

layers.description: Every layer field at this cell, by the layer's own name, as an exact read of layers[name][z][x]. Never recomputed: a re-derived field drifts from the generator by a float.

near.description: Rows by category, each ordered by distance and then by the order its writer produced it.

ley_nodes.description: magic.networks[school].nodes[]. A ley node carries a direction and no terrain node, so its node field is null.

encounter.description: One occupancy row and the travelling group it belongs to, resolved through encounters.by_node -> encounters.occupancy[].entry -> encounters.entries[], which is the index terrain_encounters built for exactly this question.

occupancy.description: Index into encounters.occupancy, so a caller can go back to the writer's own row.

from_day.description: Null on a stranded group: 'here, always', not 'here, never'.

threat_tier.description: Danger on the creature-tier rubric, one to five. Not the key-location tier, which is physical scale.

join.description: A join this read resolved, naming the site that writes the field it was resolved against. Resolving a join is writing a second implementation of it, so the mirror is checkable rather than asserted.
